title: Reflect to Reveal
use_cases: Use when designing minor characters to highlight specific personality traits of the protagonist
Implement when the narrative requires an external representation of the hero's internal conflicts
Configure when strengthening the emotional stakes through relational dynamics
Use when attempting to show rather than tell a character's flaws or strengths
content:
Secondary characters, when crafted thoughtfully as mirrors, become more than background noise—they become essential to the protagonist’s growth and to the story’s emotional weight. Through them, readers see your hero more clearly. They feel the protagonist’s fears more deeply. They understand the stakes not just intellectually, but emotionally and viscerally.

So build your mirrors with care. Polish them with nuance. And watch how they reflect not just your character’s struggles—but your story’s beating heart.
